how: An explanation nested beneath another subreddit's joke comparison cannot alone establish the host's exact styling change.
The separate prank exchange does not establish joking intent in the canvas invitation or parody across the whole host.
Repetitive host play is supported, but the narrower fake-news placement exceeds titles containing no identifiable false-news assertion.
Praise and a prospective redesign support possible reuse of styling rather than its demonstrated retention after the prank.
The surviving museum headline leaves the prank interpretation provisional because the coded title alone does not establish deception.
A surviving April Fool label supplies partial framing but does not establish a host takeover, fake content or insincere recruitment.
Takeover jokes and hypothetical recolouring do not establish an implemented takeover of the host subreddit or a fake canvas proposal.
A reversed subreddit joke does not by itself establish that calls to build on the canvas were understood as jokes.
The BTTV fragment establishes an April Fools question rather than the deleted claim's contents or the insincerity of unrelated canvas calls
Treat prank recognition as reception unless evidence identifies the room as its producer or connects it to the canvas call.
The local playful frame supports a joke response and gift without establishing fabricated news or a takeover.
Host play is not causally isolated in participants' accounts when a redirect reportedly blocks reinforcement and explicitly motivates a chat workaround.
The NFL-ban hoax and individual fan-switch jokes support April Fools play without substantiating the blind account's subreddit makeover.
Objecting to unreadable styling is not itself evidence that a user disabled or bypassed it
Providing a picture hint accommodates a player within the altered round without demonstrating that prank styling was switched off.
Questioning an April Fools prank establishes playful testing without settling the disputed authenticity of the supposed discovery.
A prank's apparent moderator authorship remains distinct from actual authorship when moderators explicitly deny sending it.
A reply calling a rental advertisement April Fools establishes the reply's attribution while leaving the advertiser's intention unresolved.
Recurring jokes and shared recognition establish play without demonstrating that the canvas calls were false or that the room was fooled.
April Fools framing applies to a channel episode-order joke without establishing a host takeover or deceptive canvas invitation.
Apply the framing to proposing and policing a late hoax, because these concepts do not establish enacted fake news or a takeover.
A threshold governing the host joke cannot establish a canvas vote, implemented moderator action, or insincerity of independent building calls.
The local-joke theme includes ordinary game comparison and cannot all be treated as fake news or a coordinated prank.
Explicitly disclosed unofficial creation does not establish deceptive fake news or an official game change.
Interpret retention only for an experienced change, keeping prospective hope for a playable release distinct from preserving an existing banner.
Reactions to a separate official joke do not establish a prank takeover or an unserious canvas proposal.
The reported play frame extends into the free weekend before the designated holiday.
Apply the reported takeover to the explicitly named affiliated server without inferring a host-subreddit takeover or joking canvas calls.
Responses to an external platform prank establish a local joke dispute without establishing host parody or a joking frame for canvas recruitment.
Joke-day framing includes usable game additions and does not establish that the later canvas call was fictitious.
The host's play frame cannot decide the truth of a particular canvas plan or disputed retrospective claim.
A late in-game prank proposal receives calendar objections without establishing an extended official licence or implemented game change.
